To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) ML techniques have been used for a wide spectrum of network management problems in various network technologies; (ii) the application of ML techniques in networking has been evolving from the early days of ML, and has reached an unprecedented maturity in the recent years; (iii) there are still open research opportunities in applying ML techniques to network problems, and in developing new ML techniques for network problems.

ML techniques have been used for a variety of network problems, including traffic prediction and forecasting, routing and classification of network traffic, congestion control, network resource and fault management and network security.
ML techniques can be used in networking to address problems in traffic prediction, routing, congestion control, network security, QoS, resource allocation, and fault management.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following questions: What is ML, and how it is applied to networking? What are the challenges and opportunities of ML in networking? What are future directions of research in ML for networking?
